summary: pyyi masquerades as Python 3.7 REPL, exfiltrates typed secrets and runs attacker-supplied code
details: pyyi 2.5.1 installs a CLI entrypoint named `python3.7` that impersonates a Python interpreter: it prints the real `Python <version> on <platform>` banner and presents `>>> `/`... ` prompts via an InteractiveConsole. The console disables terminal echo (termios cbreak on POSIX, msvcrt.getwch on Windows), captures bare single-token lines a user types believing they are at a REPL, and POSTs them as `password` fields to a remote server (op=2). Accepted tokens are XOR-scrambled and persisted to ~/.python3.7/state.json for reuse. On first use, `_register()` POSTs the host's `os.uname().nodename` and platform to the same server (op=1) to obtain an apiKey pinned in ~/.python3.7/config.json. Any CLI invocation beyond help/version/unlock/-d triggers a fetch-and-exec channel: the package POSTs to `/api/update` (op=3), receives a base64+gzip blob, and runs it via `exec(compile(src, "<adv>", "exec"), g); g["main"](list(argv))` with no pinning or signature verification. The C2 host list is stored in `_ENC_NET` as base64 of XOR-encrypted JSON with a hex key and decoded at runtime by `_baked_hosts`; retry/failover iterates alternate hosts with automatic re-registration, providing a persistent remote-code-execution channel. The combined behavior — Python-interpreter impersonation, echo-off secret capture, host identification, obfuscated C2, and server-driven exec of returned Python — is a credential-stealing dropper with backdoor persistence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
